no frame and no line written), or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, stderr empty (exit 21's document is `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`)), `viola verify` step counter (each relied row's step line ends `pass`, `absent` or `fail`, `absent` only on the `browser-tools-prompt` row when no run met the prompt, counted as a pass there alone, and a run that met that prompt prints, after a successful `stamps.json` update and before the summary, one plain ASCII stdout line, no SGR: `the browser-tools prompt stood at start; - Stamps conflict resolved: `viola verify` against the fake agent (the verify a keyed start runs included) is the only writer of `ledger/stamps.json` in tests and CI; every other writer-capable entry point leaves it byte-identical.

- The automatic verify, for a person: turn it on by setting `"verify_new_cli": true` in the viola home's `config.json` (`"v": 1`; any other value reads false); it stays off until then. What one spends: one `viola verify` run of the start's resolved `claude` — its print-mode probe on Haiku, its interactive PTY runs (their turns on the account's default model) and its `claude agents --json` read, as the `viola verify` bullet below lists — once per claude version (or per newer relied row set), before the session starts; keys typed meanwhile wait in the terminal's buffer, and Ctrl-C or TERM stops the start with no stamp and no session. A red one leaves its version's entry in `ledger/stamps.json` holding the failing rows: the start goes on unverified, and later starts print the earlier-red line and run no verify. It is cleared only by a hand-run `viola verify`, a viola build whose relied row set grows, or a newer claude version. A verify that cannot start, or is stopped, writes nothing and is no attempt; a start that finds another start verifying runs none and starts unverified.

A viola run that meets a claude version with no verify stamp can now start viola verify itself, once, when the new config.json key verify_new_cli is true; the key is off by default and in every CI home.
viola verify stays the one writer of the stamps file: the start only spawns it as a direct child with a closed argv (the pinned copy, the canonical home, the resolved program), stdin null, the start's own credential strip plan applied and VIOLA_NAME, VIOLA_DIR and VIOLA_BIN removed, tied to the start by a parent-death SIGTERM.
A new attempt lock ledger/verify.lock (0600, taken only after the strict-modes check, never the stamps writer's lock) lets one start of two verify; the other runs none. An entry already attempted and red runs no verify again, so there is no loop; a stamp short of one relied id verifies again once.
The start order gains the verify step after the endpoint bind; the folder trust record is now written after it, on the final verdict. The version gate re-reads the stamps through the strict-modes check under the lock and after the verify.
A SIGINT or SIGTERM during the start's verify TERMs the verify child, waits a 30 s grace, then KILLs it, and ends the start by the signal with no stamp, no snapshot and no session. Five fixed ASCII stderr lines (L1 to L5) say what happened, carrying only the parsed version and a closed word.
Counted: the known config keys 4 to 5, the closed spawn subjects 7 to 8 (auto-verify added), the controls table 8 to 9 entries. No dependency added, no capability claimed, nothing retired.
